name: Floor Scrubber
definition: A powered commercial floor-treatment machine that applies cleaning solution, mechanically agitates a hard floor, then collects the resulting liquid through a squeegee and vacuum-recovery system.
includedScope: Powered walk-behind, stand-on, ride-on and autonomous machines that scrub and recover liquid in the same operating cycle
Commercial and industrial hard-floor applications within the limits stated by the machine manufacturer
excludedScope: Single-disc rotary floor machines that do not recover liquid
Carpet extractors, domestic floor washers, road sweepers and sweeper-scrubbers
Model-specific repair instructions or universal component compatibility claims
headline: Floor scrubber systems, equipment types, performance metrics, components and buyer verification
description: This technical profile separates documented equipment facts from World Clean Biz procurement interpretation so buyers and engineers can compare floor scrubbers without treating unlike specifications as equivalent.
metaDescription: Floor scrubber technical profile covering scrubber dryer types, working systems, specifications, components, representative models and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This is an independent category reference, not model-specific purchasing, safety, compatibility or repair advice. Confirm the current manual, configuration, serial range, local compliance and service terms before procurement or engineering work.
heroImageAlt: Hako Scrubmaster B120 R ride-on floor scrubber shown as an official product reference
heroImageCaption: Official Hako product image of the Scrubmaster B120 R, used as a real-equipment reference for the floor scrubber category; the category includes other formats and brands.

keyFacts.label: Cleaning mechanism
keyFacts.value: Cleaning solution, rotating or orbital agitation, squeegee collection and vacuum recovery
keyFacts.evidence: Official operator documentation describes solution delivered to the floor, brushes or pads scrubbing it, and a squeegee/vacuum system recovering the dirty solution.
keyFacts.scope: Commercial walk-behind scrubbers represented by the Tennant T300 and Kärcher B 50 W manuals; other designs require model confirmation.

keyFacts.label: Operator formats
keyFacts.evidence: Reviewed official manufacturer ranges identify walk-behind, ride-on and autonomous scrubber formats; stand-on terminology appears in manufacturer product classifications.
keyFacts.scope: Terminology used by the reviewed international and US manufacturer pages; names can vary by market.

keyFacts.label: Common power source
keyFacts.value: Battery power is common; battery chemistry, voltage, charger and runtime are configuration-specific
keyFacts.evidence: Official model sources describe battery-powered configurations including lead-acid, gel/AGM and lithium-ion options.
keyFacts.scope: The reviewed Tennant, Kärcher, Nilfisk and Hako configurations; not a universal statement for every floor scrubber.

keyFacts.label: Tank arrangement
keyFacts.value: Separate fresh/solution and recovery tanks are typical in the reviewed machines
keyFacts.evidence: Official specifications list separate solution/fresh-water and recovery/dirty-water capacities.

keyFacts.label: Cleaning decks
keyFacts.value: Disc, cylindrical/roller and orbital systems appear in current commercial ranges
keyFacts.evidence: Official product pages list disc, cylindrical/roller and orbital head options across the reviewed models.
keyFacts.scope: Available options depend on exact model and configuration.

systemFlow.name: Solution delivery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Fresh-water tank, valve/pump and fluid path
systemFlow.role: Meters water or cleaning solution to the working area.
systemFlow.evidence: The reviewed manuals describe filling the solution/fresh-water tank and controlling water or detergent delivery during cleaning.
systemFlow.scope: Generic flow synthesized from the reviewed walk-behind manuals; hardware differs by configuration.

systemFlow.name: Mechanical agitation
systemFlow.componentFamily: Brush, pad driver or orbital deck
systemFlow.role: Applies motion and contact to loosen soil from the floor surface.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals and product pages identify rotating brush/pad and optional deck technologies used for scrubbing.
systemFlow.scope: Deck mechanism and suitable consumable are model- and floor-specific.

systemFlow.name: Soil suspension
systemFlow.role: Combines liquid and agitation so loosened soil can be transported toward recovery.
systemFlow.evidence: The manuals describe wet cleaning with solution and agitation before recovery of dirty liquid.
systemFlow.scope: Explanatory WCB system step based on the documented wet-cleaning cycle; chemistry and dwell requirements are not universal.

systemFlow.name: Squeegee collection
systemFlow.role: Channels liquid toward the vacuum pickup path.
systemFlow.evidence: Official documentation identifies the squeegee as part of the water-recovery system and provides blade inspection or replacement instructions.
systemFlow.scope: Reviewed walk-behind machines; blade geometry and material vary by model and application.

systemFlow.name: Vacuum recovery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Suction motor, hose and airflow path
systemFlow.role: Creates airflow to move collected liquid away from the floor.
systemFlow.evidence: The reviewed manuals describe activating suction/vacuuming and maintaining the recovery path.
systemFlow.scope: Functional category description; motor performance and airflow test methods are model-specific.

systemFlow.name: Recovery storage
systemFlow.componentFamily: Recovery tank, float/shutoff and drain path
systemFlow.role: Retains recovered liquid for controlled emptying and cleaning.
systemFlow.evidence: Official manuals and specifications identify recovery/dirty-water tanks and service procedures.
systemFlow.scope: Reviewed commercial machines; tank safeguards and drain systems differ.

variants.name: Compact
variants.taskScale: Small hard-floor areas and constrained rooms
variants.limitations: Smaller tanks and working width can increase refill and transit time.
variants.evidence: Official compact/walk-behind product positioning emphasizes confined spaces and smaller areas.
variants.scope: Category positioning, not a fixed dimensional threshold.

variants.name: Walk-behind
variants.taskScale: Small to medium areas; some larger-area models exist
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator walks behind and steers the machine
variants.spaceConstraints: Requires route width, turning room and manageable operator travel
variants.limitations: Theoretical output does not account for refill, turns, obstacles or operator pace.
variants.evidence: Tennant, Nilfisk, Kärcher and Hako identify the reviewed models as walk-behind machines.

variants.name: Stand-on
variants.taskScale: Facilities balancing travel speed with a compact operator footprint
variants.operatorRelationship: Operator stands on an integrated platform
variants.spaceConstraints: Turning envelope, ramps and platform access require site review
variants.limitations: Manufacturers do not use the term consistently across regions.
variants.evidence: Official manufacturer classification distinguishes stand-on/ride-on machines from walk-behind models.
variants.scope: Manufacturer-labelled products only; no universal category boundary is asserted.

variants.name: Ride-on
variants.taskScale: Medium to large areas and longer operating routes
variants.spaceConstraints: Confirm aisle turn, doorway, elevator, slope and transport limits
variants.limitations: Larger nominal productivity can be offset by congestion, edge work and support time.
variants.evidence: Hako positions the B120 R ride-on machine for shopping centres, production halls, stations and airports and publishes dimensions and output.
variants.scope: Hako B120 R configurations and comparable ride-on procurement questions.

variants.name: Autonomous or robotic
variants.taskScale: Repeatable routes on mapped medium-to-large hard-floor areas
variants.operatorRelationship: Automated cleaning still requires setup, supervision, exception handling and service processes
variants.spaceConstraints: Traffic, obstacles, docking access, connectivity and approved operating zones require validation
variants.limitations: Autonomy claims are model-specific and do not establish unattended suitability for every site.
variants.evidence: Kärcher describes KIRA B 50 as an autonomous scrubber dryer and states an optional docking station can refill, drain, rinse and charge it.
variants.scope: Kärcher KIRA B 50 official international materials.

performanceMetrics.name: Cleaning path
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal working width of the installed cleaning head
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Configuration-specific dimension, often reported in millimetres and inches
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: A wider path does not alone establish achieved output or fit through aisles and doors.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official model pages publish one or more cleaning paths tied to head configurations.

performanceMetrics.name: Theoretical area performance
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Nominal output derived from speed and working width under defined assumptions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not present it as practical cleaned area after turns, overlap, refill, transport and interruptions.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official pages label area performance as theoretical or estimated for reviewed models.
performanceMetrics.scope: Values retain each manufacturer's stated label and basis.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution and recovery capacity
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Indicates liquid carried and recovered before refill or drain
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal tank capacity, not usable cycle volume
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Tank size alone does not determine runtime because water flow, dosing, soil load and route differ.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official specifications list separate solution/fresh and recovery/dirty-water capacities.

performanceMetrics.name: Brush or pad pressure
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: A manufacturer-reported contact-force parameter for a named deck/configuration
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Maximum or operating pressure can use different definitions
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Higher stated pressure is not a universal cleaning-quality score and can affect floor finish and consumable wear.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Tennant publishes maximum down-pressure values for the T300 and T500 configurations.
performanceMetrics.scope: Tennant source terminology; cross-brand equivalence is not established.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime and charging
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Constrains shift coverage, opportunity charging and spare-machine planning
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Battery, charger, settings, floor resistance and accessory dependent
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not compare a maximum runtime with an achieved duty cycle or assume charger interchangeability.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official model sources state battery configurations, runtime or charging options.

performanceMetrics.name: Sound level
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Supports evaluation of occupied-space and daytime-cleaning constraints
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Reported value depends on operating mode and measurement standard
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Compare only values with compatible standards, distance, mode and uncertainty.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish sound values or low-noise modes for named configurations.
performanceMetrics.scope: Tennant T300 and Hako B25 official claims; not a category-wide threshold.

performanceMetrics.name: Turning and maneuverability
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Affects route fit, end-of-aisle turns and edge coverage
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Machine geometry, squeegee width, steering and operating context
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: A quoted turning measure must be checked against the full configured envelope and actual route.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official ride-on and autonomous materials emphasize maneuverability and confined-space application boundaries.
performanceMetrics.scope: Reviewed Hako B120 R and Kärcher KIRA B 50 materials.

applicationFit.evidence: Official product materials identify shops, supermarkets and other public-use spaces among applications for reviewed scrubbers.
applicationFit.scope: Named Tennant, Nilfisk, Hako and IEC commercial-use examples; floor and configuration remain site-specific.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: A compact or maneuverable machine may reduce aisle disruption where recovery quality and occupied-space noise are validated.
applicationFit.assessment: Match route width, opening hours, floor finish and residual-moisture performance rather than selecting on theoretical output alone.
applicationFit.basis: Official application statements plus documented size, noise and recovery attributes.
applicationFit.limitations: The reviewed sources do not establish suitability for every retail floor, traffic pattern or cleaning chemical.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Map minimum aisle and turn dimensions, then run a timed trial during representative traffic.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources identify factories, production halls and industrial locations as commercial floor-treatment environments.
applicationFit.scope: Indoor hard-floor cleaning within manufacturer limits; not explosive, corrosive or road-sweeping environments.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Route length, debris load, floor joints, slopes and service access can outweigh nominal cleaning width.
applicationFit.assessment: Evaluate pre-sweeping needs and whether a scrubber alone matches the soil profile.
applicationFit.basis: Official intended-use boundaries and large-area application statements.
applicationFit.limitations: No reviewed source supports hazardous-area use or universal oil/chemical removal.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Document soil type, slope, joints and debris; obtain written configuration approval and a site trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Manufacturer and IEC sources include hospitals or hygiene-sensitive facilities among commercial-use examples.
applicationFit.scope: General facility-floor application; infection-control protocol and chemical efficacy are outside the equipment-category evidence.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Noise, cleanability of tanks, water recovery and local infection-control procedures require joint review.
applicationFit.assessment: An equipment specification cannot substitute for a validated hygiene process.
applicationFit.basis: Official application and low-noise/hygiene feature descriptions.
applicationFit.limitations: The sources do not establish disinfection efficacy or healthcare-protocol compliance.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Have infection-control, facilities and service teams approve the complete cleaning process and trial.

applicationFit.evidence: Official sources name schools and classrooms as representative commercial environments.
applicationFit.scope: Hard floors and named model positioning; furniture density and occupied-hour rules vary.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Compact geometry, handle clearance, sound and simple controls can matter more than peak output in furnished areas.
applicationFit.assessment: Separate corridor productivity from classroom maneuverability requirements.
applicationFit.basis: Official intended-use and product application descriptions.
applicationFit.limitations: No single reviewed configuration is proven suitable for every campus surface.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Trial the machine in the tightest furnished room and longest corridor using the intended operator group.

applicationFit.evidence: Tennant's intended-use statement includes hotels and Nilfisk lists hotels among SC500 applications.
applicationFit.scope: Commercial hard-floor areas, not carpet extraction or guest-room domestic cleaning.
applicationFit.wcbAssessment: Daytime noise, elevator fit, storage, appearance and service response should be weighted alongside output.
applicationFit.assessment: A mixed-surface property may require more than one equipment category.
applicationFit.basis: Official intended-use statements and machine dimensions/features.
applicationFit.limitations: The sources do not support carpet or every specialty floor treatment.
applicationFit.buyerAction: Confirm elevator and storage dimensions and test each representative hard-floor finish.

componentStack.name: Brush, pad and cleaning deck
componentStack.role: Provides mechanical agitation at the floor interface.
criticalChecks: approved material for floor and chemistry
componentStack.evidence: Official sources list multiple deck technologies and model-specific replacement procedures.
componentStack.scope: Named configurations; no cross-machine interchangeability is implied.

componentStack.name: Squeegee assembly and blades
componentStack.role: Collects liquid behind the cleaning path and directs it to suction pickup.
variants: natural rubber or other model-approved blade materials
componentStack.evidence: Official pages and manuals identify squeegee design, blade options and maintenance.
componentStack.scope: Reviewed models; material suitability and fit are model/application-specific.

componentStack.name: Solution system
componentStack.role: Stores and meters water or cleaning solution to the deck.
componentStack.evidence: Official manuals describe solution tanks, water adjustment and optional dosing systems.
componentStack.scope: Functional grouping; exact hydraulic architecture varies.

componentStack.name: Vacuum and recovery path
componentStack.role: Moves recovered liquid through the hose into the recovery tank.
variants: Model-specific suction motor and airflow path
componentStack.evidence: Official manuals identify vacuum operation and recovery-path service points.
componentStack.scope: Reviewed walk-behind machines; airflow values are not normalized across brands.

componentStack.name: Battery and charger
componentStack.role: Supplies and replenishes electrical energy for traction, deck and recovery systems.
criticalChecks: charger part number and input supply
componentStack.evidence: Official model sources publish different battery and charger options.
componentStack.scope: Named configurations only; chemistry or charger substitution is not authorized.

componentStack.name: Traction, controls and sensors
componentStack.role: Controls movement, operating modes, safety interlocks and, on robotic machines, navigation.
criticalChecks: sensor cleaning and approved operating zone
componentStack.evidence: Official sources describe self-propelled operation, control features and autonomous navigation/docking functions.
componentStack.scope: Features vary materially by model and option package.

distinguishingSpecifications: Cleaning path: 17, 20 or 24 in / 430, 500 or 600 mm
Solution tank: 11 gal / 42 L
Estimated runtime: up to 3.8 hours
representativeModels.evidence: Tennant identifies T300 as a battery-powered walk-behind floor scrubber and publishes the listed configuration ranges.
representativeModels.scope: US page and options available when reviewed; confirm the quoted regional configuration.

distinguishingSpecifications: Cleaning path: 26, 28 or 32 in / 650, 700 or 800 mm
Solution tank: 22.5 gal / 85 L
Disc, cylindrical or orbital head options
representativeModels.evidence: Tennant identifies T500 as a walk-behind scrubber and publishes multiple cleaning paths and deck choices.
representativeModels.scope: US page and named options; not every combination is available in every market.

distinguishingSpecifications: Cleaning width: 530 mm in the SC500 manual
Solution and recovery tanks: 45 L each in the SC500 manual
Li-ion configuration product number 56394690 on the US page
representativeModels.marketScope: Nilfisk US product page with SC500 official instruction manual
representativeModels.evidence: Nilfisk lists SC500 20D Li-Ion as a walk-behind floor scrubber and the SC500 manual supplies the cited family dimensions and capacities.
representativeModels.scope: US product configuration and SC500 53 B/53R B manual family; confirm exact product-number specification before purchase.

distinguishingSpecifications: Tank volume: 50 L
D51, D60, R55 and O51 head choices
Gel/AGM or optional lithium-ion battery configurations
representativeModels.evidence: Kärcher describes B 50 W as a walk-behind scrubber dryer and lists the stated tank, head and battery choices.
representativeModels.scope: International overview; exact pack and feature availability must be confirmed by regional product number.

distinguishingSpecifications: Area performance: up to 2,300 m²/h
Optional docking station supports fresh-water fill, dirty-water empty/rinse and charging
Medium-to-large hard-floor application positioning
representativeModels.evidence: Kärcher identifies KIRA B 50 as a scrubber dryer robot and publishes its stated area performance and docking functions.
representativeModels.scope: International product-family page; site safety and autonomous operating approval remain project-specific.

distinguishingSpecifications: Working width: 43 cm
Theoretical area performance: 1,700 m²/h
Fresh and dirty water tanks: 25 L each
representativeModels.evidence: Hako identifies Scrubmaster B25 as a walk-behind scrubber-drier and publishes the cited technical data.
representativeModels.scope: Official international product page; options and battery configuration require quotation confirmation.

distinguishingSpecifications: Working widths: 70–90 cm depending on configuration
Theoretical area performance: 4,500–5,800 m²/h
Solution and recovery tanks: 120 L each
representativeModels.evidence: Hako identifies B120 R as a ride-on scrubber-drier and publishes disc/cylindrical configuration data.
representativeModels.scope: Official international configurations TB750, WB700, TB900 and WB850.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Selecting from theoretical area performance alone
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources label productivity as theoretical, estimated or up to for representative models.
procurementDecisions.scope: Published manufacturer values for named models.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Use a timed site route including turns, overlap, refill, drain and transit.
procurementDecisions.basis: Different source labels and site losses prevent a like-for-like achieved-output ranking.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not independently performance-tested these models.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Put the route, soil condition, operator and acceptance measure into the demonstration protocol.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm the installed deck, programmed speed and flow settings used during the trial.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Comparing dBA values without mode or test method
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official model sources report low-noise modes or sound values under named conditions.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Noise and residual moisture should be assessed together in the real occupied route.
procurementDecisions.basis: Low-noise operation may change machine settings and reported values are not automatically comparable.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Published values do not represent every room acoustic or floor condition.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Measure a representative pass during operating hours and document the configured mode.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Record measurement standard, distance, operating mode and squeegee/blade setup.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating maximum runtime as shift coverage
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources show multiple battery chemistries, capacities and charging options.
procurementDecisions.scope: Named configurations; local packs can differ.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Model the full energy window including cleaning load, opportunity charge, cooling and battery life policy.
procurementDecisions.basis: Runtime depends on configuration and operating settings.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Public sources do not establish the buyer's achieved duty cycle.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Require a written energy balance for the contracted battery and charger combination.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify voltage, chemistry, BMS, charger part number, input supply and warranty pairing.

procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Using cleaning width as machine width or turning clearance
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official specifications separately report working width, squeegee width and overall dimensions for reviewed models.
procurementDecisions.assessment: The route should be checked with the installed squeegee, deck and operator position.
procurementDecisions.basis: The widest and longest operating envelope can differ from nominal cleaning path.
procurementDecisions.limitations: Published dimensions do not reproduce local obstacles or turning behavior.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Measure the narrowest opening, turn and storage point, then conduct a physical route trial.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm configuration-specific width, length, turning data, slope and transport limits.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Operational design domain and exception workflow
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Equating autonomous operation with unsupervised suitability everywhere
procurementDecisions.evidence: Kärcher describes KIRA B 50 autonomous functions, sensors and optional docking support.
procurementDecisions.assessment: A deployment plan must cover mapping, traffic, obstacles, docking, alerts, supervision and manual edge work.
procurementDecisions.basis: Product capability statements do not define the buyer's complete operating environment.
procurementDecisions.limitations: WCB has not validated a deployment at the buyer's site.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run a representative pilot with logged interventions and agreed acceptance thresholds.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify safety certification scope, software/version control, connectivity, docking utilities and escalation ownership.

engineeringChecks.reason: Voltage, chemistry, BMS and charge profile must match the approved machine configuration.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm machine serial range, battery part number, charger part number, input supply and written warranty pairing.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources show configuration-specific battery and charger options.
engineeringChecks.scope: Named models; no substitution approval is implied.

engineeringChecks.reason: Working width alone does not establish brush, pad driver or orbital consumable fit.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Verify deck model, drive interface, diameter, material, speed, wear limit and exact part number.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources list multiple deck technologies and model-specific replacement instructions.
engineeringChecks.scope: Reviewed models and official accessories only.

engineeringChecks.reason: Geometry, width, blade material and adjustment affect pickup and physical fit.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Match assembly and blade part numbers to model, deck, serial range, floor/chemical and regional parts catalog.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official manuals identify model-specific squeegee service and blade options.
engineeringChecks.scope: Reviewed Tennant, Nilfisk and Kärcher families.

engineeringChecks.reason: Commercial floor-treatment machines and chargers are subject to market-specific safety and electrical requirements.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Obtain the declaration, certification markings, manual and charger input specification for the exact destination-market configuration.
engineeringChecks.evidence: IEC 60335-2-72 defines safety scope for powered commercial floor-treatment machines, including battery machines and built-in chargers.
engineeringChecks.scope: International standard scope; national adoption and legal obligations require local verification.

engineeringChecks.reason: Brand identity does not establish the local contracting, commissioning, parts or warranty provider.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Name the seller, importer, commissioning party, authorized service entity, response time, parts commitment and warranty territory in writing.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official sources direct buyers to regional contacts, authorized retailers or service support for configuration and parts.
engineeringChecks.scope: Commercial procurement action; no ownership relationship is inferred.

standards.name: IEC 60335-2-72:2021
standards.jurisdiction: International standard; adoption and legal effect vary by market
standards.applicability: Safety requirements for powered ride-on and walk-behind floor-treatment machines for commercial use within the standard's stated scope.
standards.evidence: IEC states the standard covers commercial machines used for scrubbing and related floor-treatment applications, including battery-powered machines and built-in chargers.
standards.scope: Standard scope only; purchasers must verify destination-market adoption, certification and exact machine configuration.

standards.name: IEC 62885-9:2019
standards.applicability: Methods and characteristic performance parameters for commercial walk-behind and ride-on floor scrubbers, sweepers and related floor-cleaning machines.
standards.evidence: IEC states the document lists performance parameters and measurement methods for machines within its scope.
standards.scope: The existence of the standard does not prove that a particular published specification was measured to it unless the manufacturer says so.

developments.title: Autonomous scrubber platforms add docking and mapped-route workflows
developments.summary: Kärcher's official KIRA B 50 materials describe autonomous scrubbing, sensor-based navigation and optional docking for water, waste and charging tasks.
developments.evidence: Kärcher published KIRA B 50 autonomous capability and docking functions in its official product and media materials.
developments.scope: Kärcher KIRA B 50; not a claim that all autonomous scrubbers have the same functions.

developments.title: Walk-behind platforms combine multiple deck and battery choices
developments.summary: Kärcher's B 50 W overview presents disc, roller and orbital head choices with lead-acid and optional lithium-ion configurations plus connected settings.
developments.evidence: The official B 50 W page describes the named deck, battery and connectivity options.
developments.scope: Kärcher B 50 W international overview and its later page updates.
